1	# WP-005: `makeEntry()` Type-Safety Conversion
     2	
     3	## Plan Context
     4	
     5	Address all actionable items identified in the sprint synthesis report for `2026-05-19-orchestrator-gui-polish` — six items spanning test coverage gaps, type-safety improvements, minor code hygiene, a comment fix, a validator tightening, and a `renderQueueTable` refactor to reduce accumulated complexity.
     6	
     7	## Description
     8	
     9	Convert the `makeEntry()` test factory in `orchestrator-view.test.ts` from `Record<string, unknown>` to `Partial<QueueEntry>` so the TypeScript compiler catches missing or mistyped fields at compile time rather than runtime.
    10	
    11	## Scope
    12	
    13	- `mcp-server/tests/gui/orchestrator-view.test.ts` — `makeEntry()` factory function signature and body
    14	- `mcp-server/src/gui/queue/types.ts` — referenced for the `QueueEntry` type import (read-only)
    15	
    16	## Deliverables
    17	
    18	- `makeEntry()` signature changed to `(overrides: Partial<QueueEntry> = {}): QueueEntry`
    19	- Type-only import of `QueueEntry` added to the test file
    20	- `status: 'pending' as const` added to the base object inside `makeEntry()`
    21	- All existing tests compile and pass without modification
    22	
    23	## Dependencies
    24	
    25	- WP-001
    26	
    27	## Acceptance Criteria
    28	
    29	1. `makeEntry()` has the signature `(overrides: Partial<QueueEntry> = {}): QueueEntry`.
    30	2. The file contains `import type { QueueEntry } from '../../src/gui/queue/types.js';` (or equivalent path).
    31	3. The base object returned by `makeEntry()` includes `status: 'pending' as const`.
    32	4. `npx tsc --noEmit` passes for the test file with no type errors.
    33	5. All existing tests in `orchestrator-view.test.ts` pass without modification to their call sites.
    34	
    35	## Active Pipeline Stages
    36	
    37	`implementation` → `qa` → `code-review` → `documentation`
    38	
    39	## Estimated Complexity
    40	
    41	Low
    42	
    43	## Rationale
    44	
    45	Using `Partial<QueueEntry>` gives compile-time checks without forcing tests to specify every field, remaining ergonomic for overrides. The `status: 'pending' as const` addition satisfies `QueueEntry`'s `RawQueueEntry` base type requirement.
    46	
    47	## Rejected Approaches
    48	
    49	- **Import raw `QueueEntry` type and require full objects** — rejected because it would force every test to specify all fields, making test code verbose and brittle when the interface evolves.
    50	- **Use `as unknown as QueueEntry` casts** — rejected because it defeats the purpose of type-safety; the cast silently bypasses the compiler checks this WP is trying to add.
    51	
    52	## Notes
    53	
    54	Depends on WP-001 being completed first, since both touch the same file and WP-001's new tests should be written before the factory signature changes. (Note: WP-002 in the original decomposition was remapped to WP-005 in the ledger.) The import is `import type` (erased at runtime), so there is zero runtime impact in the jsdom/vm test context.

1	# WP-006: Extract `renderQueueTable` Helpers
     2	
     3	## Plan Context
     4	
     5	Address all actionable items identified in the sprint synthesis report for `2026-05-19-orchestrator-gui-polish` — six items spanning test coverage gaps, type-safety improvements, minor code hygiene, a comment fix, a validator tightening, and a `renderQueueTable` refactor to reduce accumulated complexity.
     6	
     7	## Description
     8	
     9	Refactor `renderQueueTable` (~130 lines) by extracting three named helper functions — `_buildQueueHtml`, `_bindQueueActions`, `_mountLogPreviews` — reducing `renderQueueTable` to a ~20-line coordinating shell. This improves readability and makes individual steps unit-testable in future.
    10	
    11	## Scope
    12	
    13	- `mcp-server/gui/public/views/orchestrator.js` — `renderQueueTable` function and surrounding module scope
    14	
    15	## Deliverables
    16	
    17	- New function `_buildQueueHtml(entries)` — takes the entries array, returns the HTML string (table construction loop); ≤ 50 lines
    18	- New function `_bindQueueActions(container, entries)` — attaches DOM-based action buttons (kill/dismiss/view-project) and toggle listeners; ≤ 50 lines
    19	- New function `_mountLogPreviews(container, entries)` — starts log previews for expanded rows, pushes cleanup callbacks; ≤ 50 lines
    20	- Refactored `renderQueueTable` as a coordinating shell (~20 lines) that delegates to the three helpers
    21	- All existing tests pass without modification
    22	
    23	## Dependencies
    24	
    25	- WP-002
    26	
    27	## Acceptance Criteria
    28	
    29	1. `renderQueueTable` delegates to `_buildQueueHtml`, `_bindQueueActions`, and `_mountLogPreviews`.
    30	2. Each extracted helper is ≤ 50 lines.
    31	3. `renderQueueTable` itself is ≤ 30 lines (coordinating shell).
    32	4. All three helpers are module-scoped (IIFE-local), not added to any global namespace.
    33	5. The refactor is purely structural — the same statements execute in the same order; no behavioural change.
    34	6. All existing tests in `orchestrator-view.test.ts` continue to pass.
    35	7. Manual verification: orchestrator view loads, queue renders correctly, banner clears, scroll is stable, log previews work, action buttons (kill/dismiss/view-project) function correctly.
    36	
    37	## Active Pipeline Stages
    38	
    39	`implementation` → `qa` → `code-review` → `documentation`
    40	
    41	## Estimated Complexity
    42	
    43	High
    44	
    45	## Rationale
    46	
    47	Three agents independently flagged `renderQueueTable` complexity during the prior sprint. Extracting helpers keeps each function under 40 lines and makes unit-testing individual steps feasible in future sprints. The extraction stays within the same function scope (IIFE-local) to preserve locality.
    48	
    49	## Rejected Approaches
    50	
    51	- **Move helpers to separate files** — rejected because the frontend is vanilla JS with no module system; file-level extraction adds complexity for no practical benefit.
    52	- **Use a class** — rejected because it adds unnecessary ceremony for what is a simple function decomposition; the existing IIFE pattern is sufficient.
    53	- **Leave as-is** — rejected because three independent reviewers flagged the complexity; 130 lines in a single function exceeds the project's readability standards.
    54	
    55	## Notes
    56	
    57	Depends on WP-002 (Register statusPollTimer for Cleanup) being completed first, since WP-002 adds a cleanup line inside the function body that this refactor will restructure. Applying WP-002 first ensures the cleanup line is in place before the extraction splits the function.
